title.narrative: Sexual and reproductive health, including sexual violence services revitalized in Guantanamo

description.narrative: This proposal is aimed at two critical areas:1. Revitalize the immediate capacity of sexual and reproductive health services in the four municipalities most affected by Hurricane Oscar, including hospitals where maternal health care services are provided, family planning and STI/HIV services in community clinics and local primary health care services, and sexual violence care at the municipal level. It is expected to prevent neonatal and maternal morbidity and mortality, ensure access to contraception, provide STI treatment to young people, ensure care for victims of sexual violence.With the proposal, it will be possible to save the lives of pregnant women, people with STI/HIV, prevent unintended pregnancies, and mitigate the consequences of sexual violence.UNFPA will work with the Ministry of Health, in particular with the National Mother and Child Program and the Center for Health Promotion and Disease Prevention, and with the Federation of Cuban Women (Civil Society Organization).2. Protect specific vulnerable groups by providing hygiene and basic necessities. The project will procure and distribute culturally appropriate dignity kits to ensure hygienic and quality living conditions for pregnant women, women of reproductive age, adolescents, LGBTI, persons with disabilities and their families, and families who have completely lost their homes.UNFPA will work with the Federation of Cuban Women (FMC), taking into account that the FMC is participating in the community-level damage assessment and community brigades will be organized with the participation of the FMC and MINSAP to support the implementation of life-saving actions.Since gender inequalities are reinforced in humanitarian settings, the dignity kits will contribute to empowering women and girls, avoiding discrimination and exposure to situations that are frequently linked to harassment and expressions of gender violence.Based on UNFPA's internal experience in the implementation of the MISP, the main activities are the acquisition of sexual and reproductive kits (contraceptives, condoms, medications for complications of abortion, STI medications, post-rape treatment kits and equipment). At the same time, the proposal will ensure the acquisition of hygiene products. Awareness, communication and information initiatives will be implemented for decision makers, health providers, representatives of community organizations and beneficiaries.Gender mainstreaming and the human rights approach are strategic axes for the objectives of this project.These actions are focused on the four affected municipalities: Maisi, Baracoa, Imias and San Antonio del Sur.Support for the maintenance of SRH services will be complemented by USD 170,000 already approved from the agency's emergency funds and usd 28 000 are redirected from the Program's regular resources. UNFPA is in constant exchange with PAHO, leader of the health cluster, to ensure the complementarity of the actions carried out and the objectives of the proposal. In this case, UNFPA will be supporting, jointly with the health sector, the area of SRH, both the sustainability of life-saving services and the availability of supplies, including Dignity Kits, focusing on pregnant women, adolescents, trans people, among other groups in conditions of greater vulnerability. It also includes communication and information actions also aimed at preventing maternal mortality and morbidity, sexually transmitted infections, and gender-based violence. Related to procurement, UNFPA will acquire the IARH kits, complementing the scope of procurement with emergency funds. Equipment will also be purchased for primary and secondary level maternal health services.
